mainTopic: שתי שערות (location, מיאון, length) and whether a כתם can lead to זיבה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge from the story of איוב, where ה׳ says every hair has its own follicle. The גמרא answers that this is true only of the head, not the body. שמואל and a ברייתא say the two hairs of adulthood can be in different places. רב חסדא explains that the רבנן require both hairs in one place. A ברייתא then gives four opinions on how long a girl can do מיאון, and רבי עקיבא firmly holds to two hairs. A new משנה gives three measures for how long the two hairs must be, and the הלכה follows all of them to be strict. The next משנה asks whether a כתם can make a woman a זבה. The גמרא explains the view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, works through רבא's argument with the רבנן about a three-גריסין stain, and ends with a ברייתא on how big a stain must be to raise a concern of זיבה.

steps.title: ה׳ tells איוב that every hair has its own follicle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge from the story of איוב‎. ה׳ says He gave every hair its own follicle, so how can two hairs grow from one follicle?
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ answered איוב from the storm and said: You fool! I made many hairs on a person's head, and I gave each hair its own follicle so two hairs would not feed from the same one. If they did, it would weaken a person's eyesight. If I never mixed up one follicle with another, would I mix up איוב with אויב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to the earlier statement that two hairs in one follicle count. ה׳'s words to איוב suggest that two hairs never come from one follicle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב had complained that ה׳ mixed up his name איוב with אויב (enemy). ה׳ answers that He is so exact that He never confuses even one follicle with another, since each hair has its own. If that is true, the case of two hairs from one follicle should not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: A small pit; here, the follicle (root hole) a hair grows from
A single hair
Draw nourishment, literally 'nurse'
Enemy
Weakens his eyesight

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of the challenge. The question itself, and the earlier statement that two hairs in one follicle count, came right before this text.

phrases.english: Job out of the tempest, and said” to him:
Greatest fool in the world!

phrases.aramaic: הַרְבֵּה נִימִין בָּרָאתִי בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: I created many hairs on a person's head,
and for each and every hair
I created its own separate follicle,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ שְׁתַּיִם יוֹנְקוֹת מִגּוּמָּא אַחַת,
phrases.english: so that two should not draw nourishment from one follicle,
for if two drew nourishment from one follicle,
it would weaken a person's eyesight.
If I never confused one follicle with another,
would I confuse “Iyov” with “oyev” (enemy)?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that two hairs growing from one follicle count as שתי שערות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ says every hair has its own follicle, so two hairs from one follicle should never happen.

steps.title: The head is different from the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'one hair per follicle' rule only applies to the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. One statement is about the body, and the other is about the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. On the body two hairs can come from one follicle, but on the head each hair has its own follicle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s words to איוב were about hairs on the head, which is why they mention eyesight. The sign of adulthood is about hair on the body, so the two statements are about different places and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources talk about different cases
The body
The head

steps.whatToRemember: Two hairs in one follicle can count as a sign of adulthood, because on the body this can happen. The 'each hair has its own follicle' rule is only about the head.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about the body, that is about the head.
phrases.notes: The ruling that two hairs in one follicle count is about the body. ה׳'s words to איוב are about the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא הא בגופא הא ברישא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from איוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: the two sources speak about different parts of the body.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ה׳'s words seemed to mean no hair anywhere could share a follicle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only head hairs each have their own follicle. On the body two hairs can share one, so they can count.

steps.title: The two hairs do not need to be next to each other
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the two hairs count even if each one is in a different spot in the private area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The two hairs that the חכמים spoke about count even if one is on the area above the organ and one is on the testicles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל: the two hairs that show adulthood do not have to grow in the same spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about two hairs that are very close, even in one follicle. Now שמואל goes the other way and says that even hairs in two different spots of the private area join together to make שתי שערות.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs, the sign that a boy or girl has become an adult in halacha
Literally 'spoon'; here, the spoon-shaped area above the male organ
Testicles

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
The two hairs that they spoke about,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים, who said two hairs are the sign of adulthood.

phrases.english: count even if one is on the spoon-shaped area
and one is on the testicles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל שתי שערות שאמרו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question: must the two hairs be in the same place?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two hairs in different spots of the private area, one on the כף and one on the ביצים, together count as שתי שערות.

steps.title: A ברייתא that says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יהודה that also lets the two hairs be in different places, even far apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: The two hairs count even if one is on her back and one on her belly, or one on the knuckles of her hand and one on the knuckles of her foot. These are the words of רבי שמעון בן יהודה of כפר עכו, who said it in the name of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports שמואל with a ברייתא that also says the two hairs may be in separate places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes even further than שמואל. It counts hairs on the back and belly, and even one on the hand and one on the foot. The גמרא names the author of this view, which sets up the question of what the other חכמים hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this, a phrase used to bring support
Her belly
The knuckles (joints) of her fingers or toes

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a baraita:
The two hairs that they spoke about,
count even if one is on her back and one is on her belly,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת עַל גַּבֵּי קִשְׁרֵי אֶצְבְּעוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל יָד
phrases.english: or one is on the knuckles of her hand

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת עַל גַּבֵּי קִשְׁרֵי אֶצְבְּעוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל רֶגֶל —
phrases.english: and one is on the knuckles of her foot.

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of the village of Akko,
who said it in the name of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that the two hairs need not be next to each other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון, which counts hairs in separate places.

steps.title: What do the רבנן hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other חכמים say about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do the רבנן say?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא named one חכם as the author, so the גמרא asks what the other חכמים hold. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming רבי שמעון בן יהודה as the source suggests that others disagree. The גמרא wants to know the view of the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The other חכמים, often the majority view

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: what do the other חכמים hold about where the two hairs must be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the other side of the view in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The view of the רבנן on whether the two hairs may be in separate places.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the רבנן require both hairs in one place
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the רבנן only count the two hairs if they are in the same place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Only when the two hairs are in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the רבנן disagree with רבי שמעון בן יהודה. For them, the two hairs must grow in one place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two views. רבי שמעון בן יהודה, and שמואל along with him, lets the hairs be in different spots. The רבנן say two hairs in separate places do not join together.

keyTerms.meaning: Not until they are; only when
One place

steps.whatToRemember: There is a disagreement. רבי שמעון בן יהודה, and שמואל like him, counts two hairs even in different places. The רבנן, as רב חסדא explains, require both hairs in one place.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Not until the two hairs are in one place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חסדא עד שיהו שתי שערות במקום אחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the רבנן's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן only count the two hairs if both are in one place.

steps.title: Four opinions on when a girl loses the right of refusal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four opinions on how long a girl can still do מיאון: two hairs (רבי מאיר), more black than white (רבי יהודה), hair surrounding the עטרה (רבי יוסי), or the area filled with hair (בן שלקות).
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Until when can a girl refuse? Until she grows two hairs, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: until the black hair covers more than the bare skin. רבי יוסי says: until hair surrounds the nipple ring. בן שלקות says: until the area is filled with hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives four different time limits for when a young girl can still cancel her marriage through מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four opinions use signs of physical growth, but each one sets a later point than the last. רבי מאיר's two hairs is the earliest sign. The others give the girl more time, all the way to בן שלקות's fully grown hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing מיאון: a young girl married off by her mother or brothers cancels the marriage by refusing
Two hairs, the basic sign of physical adulthood
Until the black hair covers more than the bare skin
Literally 'crown'; here, the ring around the nipple
Become filled with hair

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד מָתַי הַבַּת מְמָאֶנֶת?
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Until when can a girl refuse?
Until she grows two hairs;
this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּרְבֶּה הַשָּׁחוֹר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until the black becomes greater.
phrases.notes: He means the area covered by black hair is bigger than the bare white skin.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁתַּקִּיף הָעֲטָרָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Until hair surrounds the nipple ring.
Ben Shelakot says: Until the area is filled with hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד מָתַי הַבַּת מְמָאֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the two hairs must be (steps 3-6) to the related question of the time limit for מיאון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four views on the end of מיאון: two hairs, majority black, hair around the עטרה, or full hair growth.

steps.title: A challenge sent to רבי עקיבא about the two-hairs view
steps.stepSummary: חנינא בן חכינאי asks רבי שמעון to challenge רבי עקיבא: if he says 'two hairs,' remind him that בן שלקות testified in יבנה that the limit is full hair growth, and nobody objected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: חנינא בן חכינאי found me in צידן and said: When you get to רבי עקיבא, ask him until when a girl can refuse. If he says until two hairs, tell him: But בן שלקות testified in front of all of you in יבנה that it is until the area is filled with hair, and you said nothing to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון tells a story. Someone sent him with a prepared challenge against the 'two hairs' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the חכמים stayed silent when בן שלקות testified in public at יבנה. Silence like that looks like agreement. So how can רבי עקיבא now say two hairs?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…, opening a challenge
Testified, gave formal testimony about a law
In the presence of
The town where the great בית מדרש of the חכמים sat

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon said:
Ḥanina ben Ḥakhinai found me in Tzaidan,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מַגִּיעַ אֵצֶל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: and said: When you reach Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: אֱמוֹר לוֹ: עַד מָתַי הַבַּת מְמָאֶנֶת?
phrases.english: say to him: Until when can a girl refuse?

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֹאמַר לָךְ: עַד שֶׁתָּבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת,
phrases.english: If he says to you: Until she grows two hairs,

phrases.aramaic: אֱמוֹר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא בֶּן שְׁלָקוֹת הֵעִיד
phrases.english: say to him: But didn't Ben Shelakot testify
in the presence of all of you in Yavne that it is until the area is filled with hair,
and you did not say anything to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא בֶּן שְׁלָקוֹת הֵעִיד בְּמַעֲמַד כּוּלְּכֶם בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses בן שלקות's opinion from step 7 to attack the two-hairs view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that מיאון ends at two hairs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בן שלקות testified publicly in יבנה, and the חכמים' silence suggests they accepted his view.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא dismisses the challenge and keeps the two-hairs rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that he does not know what כלכול is and does not know any בן שלקות. The limit stays at two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came to רבי עקיבא, he said to me: This 'filling' I don't know what it is. בן שלקות I don't know. Until when can a girl refuse? Until she grows two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes the challenge away completely and repeats that the limit is two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue about the silence at יבנה. He simply refuses to recognize the term or the person, so the testimony carries no weight for him. The two-hairs rule stands firm.

keyTerms.meaning: I don't know what it is
I don't recognize (him)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא holds firmly that a girl can do מיאון only until she grows two hairs, and he rejects בן שלקות's testimony.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁבָּאתִי אֵצֶל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אָמַר לִי:
phrases.english: When I came to Rabbi Akiva, he said to me:
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון is still telling the story here.

phrases.english: This 'filling with hair', I do not know what it is;
Ben Shelakot, I do not know him;
until when can a girl refuse?
Until she grows two hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 8 by rejecting its source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge built on בן שלקות's testimony
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The term כלכול and the witness בן שלקות are unknown to רבי עקיבא, so the testimony has no authority.

steps.title: How long the two hairs must be
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the two hairs mentioned for פרה אדומה, נגעים, and everywhere else must be long enough to bend tip to root (רבי ישמעאל), to nip with a fingernail (רבי אליעזר), or to cut with scissors (רבי עקיבא).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The two hairs mentioned for the פרה אדומה, for נגעים, and everywhere else count only if they are long enough to bend their tips to their roots, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי אליעזר says: long enough to nip with a fingernail. רבי עקיבא says: long enough to be cut with scissors.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks how long a hair must be to count as one of the 'two hairs' in halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same minimum length applies in every place where the Torah or the חכמים speak of two hairs. The three opinions give three different measures of length, each tied to a physical test.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה, which becomes unfit if it has two hairs of another color
Leprous marks, which become impure if two white hairs grow in them
To bend their tips over to their roots
To nip off with a fingernail
A pair of scissors

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets one shared length rule for 'two hairs' across very different areas of halacha.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The two hairs that are mentioned regarding the red heifer,
and regarding leprous marks, and those mentioned in every place,
phrases.notes: This includes the two hairs that show a boy or girl has become an adult.

phrases.english: must be long enough to bend their tops to their roots;
this is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לִקְרוֹץ בַּצִּיפּוֹרֶן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Long enough to nip them with a fingernail.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ נִיטָּלוֹת בְּזוּג.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: Long enough to be cut with a pair of scissors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the size of the two hairs discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three measures for a hair to count: bendable tip to root, nippable with a fingernail, or cuttable with scissors.

steps.title: The ruling: follow every opinion to be strict
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting מר עוקבא, rules that the הלכה follows all three opinions about hair length, whichever is strictest in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: The הלכה follows all of them, to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on the משנה from Step 10, which had three opinions on how long the two hairs must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single opinion wins outright. In each case we use whichever opinion gives the stricter result. Sometimes that means treating short hairs as real hairs, and sometimes it means waiting for longer hairs.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law we follow
According to the words of all of them
To be strict

steps.whatToRemember: For the length of the two hairs, we take the strictest of the three opinions (רבי ישמעאל, רבי אליעזר, רבי עקיבא) in each situation.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean one opinion is the law. It means we pick whichever of the three is strictest for the case at hand, so the 'winning' opinion can change from case to case.

phrases.english: Gemara

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says that Mar Ukva says:
The halakha follows the words of all of them, to be stringent.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the three opinions on hair length in the משנה from Step 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling for the three-way dispute in Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For hair length, follow whichever opinion is most stringent in each case.

steps.title: New משנה: does a stain raise a concern of זוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a woman who finds a כתם has a ruined count and must worry about זוב. The חכמים say stains never raise a זוב concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who sees a stain has a ruined count, and she must worry about זוב. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: stains never raise a זוב concern.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: a woman who finds a blood stain on her clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she does not know when the stain's blood came out, she cannot tell where she stands in her count of נדה days and זבה days. רבי מאיר says she must therefore worry that she may be a זבה. The חכמים say a stain alone can never make her a זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on clothing, not blood seen leaving the body
Thrown off; her count of days is ruined
She must be concerned or worry
Flow of blood outside the normal time, which can make a woman a זבה

phrases.english: Mishnah
A woman who sees a stain
this woman is thrown off
phrases.notes: She doesn't know when the blood came out, so her count of days is thrown off.

phrases.english: and she must be concerned about the flow of a zava,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
Stains do not raise any concern of zav flow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a stain ruins her count and raises a זוב concern. חכמים: stains never raise a זוב concern.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific sage the unnamed חכמים in the משנה are.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the unnamed חכמים are, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says חכמים without a name. The גמרא wants to know which known sage holds this view, so we can find his fuller wording elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
The Sages, an unnamed group opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara
Who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to identify the חכמים of the משנה in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the sage behind the חכמים' opinion.

steps.title: They are רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. A ברייתא quotes him saying stains don't raise a זוב concern, but sometimes stains can lead to זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: Stains do not raise a זוב concern, but sometimes stains bring a woman to זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים are רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, and brings a ברייתא with his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first half matches the חכמים in the משנה exactly. But it adds a second half saying stains can sometimes lead to זיבה. That sounds like the opposite, and it needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of being a זבה
Sometimes
Bring a person to; lead to

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the second half as taking back the first half. He still holds that a stain by itself doesn't make her a זבה. Step 15 explains the 'sometimes.'

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
Stains do not raise a concern of zav flow.
But sometimes stains bring her to ziva.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, whose ברייתא says stains don't raise a זוב concern, yet sometimes lead to זיבה.

steps.title: Which stains can lead to זיבה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס gives two cases where stains can lead to זיבה. In the first, she wore three checked garments and found a stain on each. In the second, she saw blood from her body on two days and found a stain on a garment on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If she wore three garments that she had checked and found a stain on them, or if she saw blood two days and then found a stain on one garment, those are the stains that bring a woman to זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from step 14 and explains what רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס meant when he said that "sometimes stains can lead to זיבה."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זבה needs three days of seeing blood. In רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view, a single stain on a single garment does not count for that, but stains can still help add up to three days. That can happen when each of three separate garments has a stain, or when two real days of bleeding are followed by one stained garment.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? It introduces an explanation of what was just said.
Garments that were checked beforehand and known to be clean
The status of a זבה, a woman who sees blood three days in a row outside her normal time
A blood stain found on a garment, not seen coming from the body

phrases.english: How so?
If she wore three garments that had been checked by her,
and she found a stain on them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁרָאֲתָה שְׁנֵי יָמִים וְחָלוּק אֶחָד —
phrases.english: or she saw blood for two days, and then a stain on one garment —

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן הַכְּתָמִים הַמְּבִיאִין לִידֵי זִיבָה.
phrases.english: these are the very stains that bring her to זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? לָבְשָׁה שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלוּקוֹת הַבְּדוּקוֹת לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 14 by spelling out its last clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stains can lead to זיבה in two cases: one stain on each of three checked garments, or two days of seeing blood from the body plus one stained garment.

steps.title: Why is the second case needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a question. If we already worry about זיבה when all three days are only stains, it should be obvious that we worry when two of the days were real bleeding from her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, with three garments, where she did not see anything from her body, we still worry. Do we even need to be told about two days plus one garment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for saying something that seems obvious and unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three stains with no actual bleeding is the weaker case. Two real days of bleeding plus one stain is the stronger case. If we worry in the weak case, we should surely worry in the strong one, so why say it?

keyTerms.meaning: "Now that... is it even necessary?" The case being asked about is an obvious step up from what was already said.
We are concerned, we take it into account
From her body, meaning blood she actually saw coming out

phrases.english: Now, with three garments,
where she does not see it from her body — we are concerned;
two days and one garment — is it even necessary to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלוּקוֹת, דְּלָאו מִגּוּפַהּ קָחָזְיָא — חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second case of the ברייתא in step 15 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second case in the ברייתא: two days of seeing blood plus one stained garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three-garment case already teaches the bigger point, so the two-days-plus-one case is obvious and seems not worth saying.

steps.title: The second case teaches that she is only a doubtful זבה
steps.stepSummary: The second case is needed. Otherwise you might think that two real days plus a stain make her a definite זבה, whose offering gets eaten. The ברייתא teaches that she is only a doubtful זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that in any case like this, she brings an offering and it is eaten. So the ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that the second case teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not about whether we worry. It is about how strongly we worry. Since two of the days were real bleeding, you might think she is a definite זבה whose bird offering is eaten. The ברייתא, by putting this case next to the three-stain case, shows that she is still only a doubtful זבה, so her offering is not eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have said..." This introduces the mistaken idea that the ruling is coming to prevent.
An offering that is eaten. That happens only when she is definitely a זבה, not just a doubtful one.
"It teaches us" that the mistaken idea is wrong

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the answer is "we worry more in the second case." The point is the reverse: even in the second case, she is only a doubtful זבה.

phrases.english: You might have said,
that in any case like this,
she brings an offering and it is eaten,
phrases.notes: The offering is eaten only when she is surely a זבה. If she is just a maybe, the offering is not eaten.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, כֹּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case teaches something new about the level of doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two real days plus one stain would make her a definite זבה, whose offering is eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is only a doubtful זבה, so her offering is not eaten.

steps.title: רבא: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס has the stronger argument
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues against the רבנן using their own logic. A stain smaller than three גריסין in one place doesn't worry us, because we say it came from fewer than three days. In the same way, a stain of three גריסין could be explained as two and a half from her body and the rest louse blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: on this point, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס beat the רבנן. Why don't we worry about less than three גריסין in one place? Because we say she saw it over two days. Then with three גריסין in one place, let us also say she saw two and a half from her body, and the rest is louse blood that came along with the dirt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a reason why רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view, that a single stain does not cause worry about זיבה, wins out over the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that we don't worry about זיבה when a stain is smaller than three גריסין in one place. רבא argues that the same "explain it away" logic works even for a full three-גריסין stain in one place. We can say most of it came from her body over less than three days, and a small bit is louse blood, so even that stain should not raise a זיבה concern.

keyTerms.meaning: He beat them, he won the argument against them
A split bean, a standard measure for the size of a stain
Blood from a louse, a common way to explain a stain as not coming from her
Dirt or filth

steps.whatToRemember: רבא argues that a three-גריסין stain in one place can be explained as less than three days of blood plus a bit of louse blood, so it should not make her a possible זבה. That is why רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס has the stronger argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the position of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס follows from reasoning the רבנן themselves already accept.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא זַכִּנְהוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: On this point רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס beat the רבנן:
phrases.notes: The רבנן here are the ones who agree with רבי מאיר from step 12 that stains can raise a worry about זיבה.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה גְּרִיסִין בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: what is different about less than three split beans in one place,
that we are not concerned?
Because we say she saw it over two days.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה גְּרִיסִין בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד נָמֵי נֵימָא:
phrases.english: Then with three split beans in one place, let us also say:
she saw two and a half of it from her body,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידָּךְ אַגַּב זוּהֲמָא דַּם מַאֲכוֹלֶת הוּא.
phrases.english: and the rest is louse blood that came along with the dirt.
phrases.notes: He means the leftover half bean of blood doesn't count, so the stain adds up to less than three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּהָא זַכִּנְהוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס) and argues for the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן's own reasoning for small stains also applies to a three-גריסין stain in one place, so such a stain should not raise a worry about זיבה.

steps.title: The Rabbis' reply: a stain that can be split by day is not blamed on a louse
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer רבא's argument. Since the stain is big enough to give each of the three days a גריס and a bit, we do not blame part of it on a louse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would the רבנן answer? Since the stain can be divided so that each day gets a גריס and a little more, we do not blame it on a louse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן would answer רבא's argument and gives their reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small stain in one place is blamed on fewer days because it is too small to cover three days. A stain of three גריסין and a bit is different. It can be fully divided into three days, each with a full-sized stain, so the רבנן see no reason to blame a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: A split bean's size plus a little more. This is the smallest size of a stain that counts.
To divide or split up
We attribute (the stain to another cause)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This is a short question: how would the רבנן answer רבא's argument?

phrases.english: Since it is possible to divide it
into a split bean and a bit for each day
we do not attribute it (to a louse).
phrases.notes: The word 'louse' is left unsaid. He means blaming part of the stain on דם מאכולת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן against רבא's argument in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a stain too small to split by day from one big enough to split
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Just as a small stain is blamed on fewer days, a three-גריסין stain could be partly blamed on a louse.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the stain can be divided into a full stain for each day, we do not look for another cause.

steps.title: Does רבי חנינא worry about three stains on one garment?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's argument suggests that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס worries when the stains are in three places. But he himself said he only worries with three separate garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view, it is only three גריסין in one place that does not worry us. That suggests that three places would worry us. But didn't you say that three garments, yes, but three places, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's argument. It reads it as the view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס and finds a contradiction with his own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's argument only lets off a stain in one place. That implies stains in three places on one garment would raise a זיבה concern. But רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס clearly limited the concern to three different garments, so three spots on one garment should not worry us.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned (here, that she may be a זבה)
Garments or robes
Places or spots (on the same garment)
But didn't you say. This points out a contradiction.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus,
three split beans' worth in one place
is where we are not concerned,
which implies that in three places, we are concerned.
But didn't you say:
on three garments, yes (we are concerned),
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא in step 15, about three checked garments.

phrases.english: in three places, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a problem with רבא's argument as the view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's argument about three גריסין in one place, taken as רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What רבא's argument implies (three places cause concern) contradicts רבי חנינא's stated rule (only three garments cause concern).

steps.title: רבי חנינא was arguing on the Rabbis' own terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס himself only worries with three garments. He told the רבנן: 'Even by your view, at least admit that one stain of three גריסין can be partly blamed on a louse.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking to the רבנן by their own view. By my view: three garments, yes; three places, no. But by your view, at least admit to me that where she saw three גריסין in one place, we say two and a half came from her body, and the rest is louse blood, because of the dirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The argument about one place was not רבי חנינא's own view. It was a point he made to the רבנן based on their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's real rule stays the same: only three separate garments raise a זיבה concern. The argument about one stain was a 'let's grant your view' move. Even if the רבנן worry about three places, they should at least let off a single stain of three גריסין, since part of it can be blamed on a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words. Arguing by the other side's own view.
At least admit to me
Two and a half
Dirt or filth
Louse blood

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס only worries about זיבה with three separate garments. His argument about one stain was made to the רבנן on their own terms.

phrases.english: He was speaking to them by the Rabbis' own words:
According to me:
on three garments, yes,
in three places, no,
but according to you,
at least admit to me
that where she saw
three split beans' worth in one place,
that we say: two and a half
she saw from her body,
and the rest
is louse blood, because of the dirt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument on the other side's terms. The statement was a 'by your view' point, not the speaker's own position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one-place argument shows that רבי חנינא worries about three places on one garment.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא himself only worries with three garments. The one-place argument was aimed at the רבנן.

steps.title: The Rabbis' reply, repeated against רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the רבנן's reply, now as their answer to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's argument. A stain that can be split into a full stain for each day is not blamed on a louse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Since the stain can be divided so that each day gets a גריס and a little more, we do not blame it on a louse.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the argument is known to be רבי חנינא's, the גמרא repeats how the רבנן answer him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as step 19, but now it answers רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס directly. The רבנן do not accept his request. A stain big enough to give each of three days its own full stain still raises a זיבה concern.

keyTerms.meaning: For each day
Since, because
There is, it is possible

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: a stain of three גריסין and a bit in one place can still lead to a זיבה concern, because it can be divided among three days. רבי חנינא: only stains on three separate garments do.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
Since it is possible to divide it
into a split bean and a bit for each day
we do not attribute it (to a louse).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's answer to רבי חנינא's argument from step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the request to split the stain between her body and a louse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן should at least admit that one three-גריסין stain can be partly blamed on a louse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it can be fully divided among three days, the רבנן do not blame a louse.

steps.title: A stain big enough for three days makes her worry
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a stain large enough to split into three pieces, each a גריס and a bit, makes her worry that she is a זבה. A smaller stain does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If a woman finds a stain, and it is big enough to split into three parts, each the size of a גריס and a bit, she must worry. If it is not that big, she does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a clear size rule for a single stain. If it can be split into three full-sized pieces, she must worry. If it cannot, she need not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To become a זבה, a woman must see blood on three days. One stain can only point to three days if each day gets its own full-sized piece, which is at least a גריס and a bit. This matches the view of the רבנן we just saw: a stain that can be split into full pieces for each day is not blamed on a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment, where she did not feel it come out
The size of a split bean plus a little more. This is the smallest stain that counts as her own blood.
To divide. Here it means splitting the one stain in our minds into three parts.
She must be concerned, meaning she must treat herself as a possible זבה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who sees a stain,
if it has enough in it to be divided into
three גריסין, each being a גריס and a bit more,
she must be concerned,
phrases.notes: Concerned that she may be a זבה, since three days of seeing blood is what makes a זבה.

phrases.english: and if not, she need not be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that states as a rule the idea the רבנן used in step 22: a stain that can be split into full pieces for three days counts as three days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single stain that can be divided into three pieces, each a גריס and a bit, makes her worry that she is a זבה. A smaller stain does not.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: she worries in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן אגרא, quoting רבי יוסי, disagrees with the first opinion. He says she must worry whether or not the stain is big enough to split into three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן אגרא says in the name of רבי יוסי: In both cases, big stain or smaller stain, she must worry.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא argues with the first. It says she must worry even when the stain is too small to split into three full pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion needed room for three full pieces, one for each day. רבי יוסי makes her worry even without that much room. The usual explanation is that two sightings could add up to three days if one of them was at בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, which may belong to two days. The ברייתא itself just gives the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that. Here it means both the large stain and the smaller stain.
A woman who saw blood on three days in a row outside her normal time. She has a stricter level of טומאה.
Twilight, which is a doubtful time that may belong to either of two days. This is the usual reason given for רבי יוסי's view.

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: she worries only if the stain can be split into three pieces of a גריס and a bit each. רבי יוסי: she worries even if it is smaller.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra says in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
Both in this case and in that case, she must be concerned.
phrases.notes: "This" is the stain big enough to split into three, and "that" is the smaller stain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא. It is stricter than the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She must worry that she is a זבה even when the stain is too small to be divided into three pieces of a גריס and a bit each.
